transcript: If you're not sleeping more than five hours a night, you need to hear this. Your body has not forgotten how to sleep. It has simply forgotten how to feel safe. In ancient wisdom, we say, the heart is the emperor, and the emperor needs a quiet palace to rest. When you sleep too little, your emperor is living in exile. It is not just that you are tired. You are in permanent alert, waiting for a danger that does not exist in a place that should be your sanctuary. I want to teach you a small but deeply powerful practice. Save this video and watch it every night for one week until your body begins to remember its natural rhythm. Before you close your eyes, place one hand on your chest and the other on your lower belly. Inhale through your nose for four seconds, not into your lungs, but deep into your belly, into the point we call the dantian, your center of gravity. Hold the breath for just one brief moment, then exhale slowly for six seconds through slightly pursed lips. That long exhale is the only signal your nervous system truly understands. It tells your body the war is over, that it can drop its guard, do not try to force sleep to come. Sleep is like a butterfly. If you chase it, it flies away. If you sit quietly, it lands on you. The problem is not the hours you spend in bed, but the heavy weight you carry into it. Practice this breath. Do not look for a miracle on the first night. Simply be present. Silence is not the absence of noise. It is the absence of resistance. Give yourself permission to disappear for a few hours. Write in the comments. Rest. If you are going to try this tonight, and if you feel that the problem is not just one night, but that you have spent years without sleeping in peace, without releasing what you carry, without giving your body permission to let its guard down, I spent over 20 years learning in silence how to calm the mind and body from the root, and everything I know is inside the way back to stillness. The link is in my profile.
